svg.text: D Standalone sub-mechanisms (1 of 2) — holding, feeling, pouring, cutting
Each panel loops on its own. Passive geometry buys the dexterity a human hand would need.
source: D-manipulator.md section 7
N6 in D-spit-stations · N9 in D-sock-arm · N12 in D-wall-puck · N17 in D-twin-turret
N1 Ice chuck (freeze workholding)
A wet cut face placed on the cold patch freezes on in 5–10 s: a
flat, crevice-free fixture. Freezing 0.5 mm of tissue is
invisible in cooked food.
N2 Fakir hand

g.text: tines Ø1.5 × 40 at 5 mm pitch; the blade runs in the lanes

svg.text: Holding and cutting no longer compete for space, and the blade
position is referenced to the holder. Stripping: lift against the
flat of the blade.
N3 The board feels
The hand can then be a plain position-controlled axis set: touch-
down, press force and cut-through come from the board. About 60
N4 Tip-bar pour
Every vessel has a hook lip on one side and a bail pocket on the
other. Hung on a fixed bar, lifting the bail pours it to 120° —
no tilt actuator, no pouring wrist.
N5 Snap C-ring for Rouladen
No piercing, no aiming a pin: pushed on from above, the ring
springs closed round the roll. Two per Roulade, reusable, removed
at plating by a hook.
N10 Rolling-disc knife

g.text: free-running Ø100 disc: cuts by translation only
a gang of five at 3 mm pitch minces herbs

svg.text: No draw stroke, no tip to steer: ideal for a Cartesian hand.
Needs a board or a belt it may touch.
